subject: Pilot scoping: streaming vs batching economics and SLOs - post-call recap
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@veloxai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scoping: streaming vs batching economics and SLOs - post-call recap

Hi Aisha,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the VeloxAI product flows. Quick recap from our side and the asks to move to a scoped pilot. I kept this short and action-oriented.

Call highlights
- Primary use case: conversational assistance in the product and async summarization for support tickets.
- Target user experience: interactive chat (low latency) + regular bulk jobs (throughput-focused).
- Initial complexity: one LLM family (open-weights candidate), some reranking on top.

Key numbers we need to finalize pricing/architecture (please confirm):
1) Expected monthly token volume (combined input+output) for pilot months 1-3
2) Avg tokens per request (input vs output split)
3) Peak concurrent interactive sessions (RPS / concurrency) and expected steady-state QPS
4) Budget target range for pilot (monthly) and target $ / 1M tokens you’d like to land on
5) Latency SLOs: P95 target for interactive chat (ms) and whether 99th matters for you

Our preliminary recommendations (based on call):
- Mixed routing: route interactive requests to streaming-optimized endpoints (dedicated or high-priority hosted tier) to hit P95 latency targets; route batch/async jobs to batched, cost-optimized paths.
- Streaming for UI: best for <300-400ms P95; batching for non-interactive workloads reduces unit costs by 20–50% depending on batch sizes.
- Quantization / model variant: moving to int8 or 4-bit quantized runtime reduces cost per 1M tokens materially; we’ll map compatible model variants in the pilot.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short pilot plan and a cost model template — please fill the token-volume cells and return.

Next steps
- Aisha / Ravi: send the numbers above by Mon (17 Aug) so we can lock a pilot scope and produce a modeled cost table.
- Redwood (Grace + Vivek): we'll produce 2 pilot options: (A) latency-first (higher unit cost, lower P95) and (B) cost-first (batched-heavy, lower unit cost) with estimated $ / 1M token ranges.
- Schedule: propose a 30-min follow-up on Tue to review modeled numbers and agree rollout.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pilot-plan.pdf, cost_model_template.csv
From: Aisha Patel <aisha@veloxai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@veloxai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scoping: streaming vs batching economics and SLOs - post-call recap

Thanks Jonas — solid recap. Numbers below (pilot months 1–3, rough):
- Monthly combined tokens: ~150,000,000 tokens/month (150M)
- Avg tokens per request: ~300 input / ~900 output => ~1,200 combined average
- Peak interactive concurrency: ~300 concurrent sessions (spiky during business hours); steady-state QPS ~35
- Budget target for pilot: $8k–$15k / month (we want sub-$10k if quality remains identical)
- Target unit econ: ideally <= $10 / 1M tokens; willing to go to $12 with guaranteed latency
- Latency: P95 target for interactive UI is 300ms; P99 not a hard blocker but would like visibility.

Questions from our side:
1) Can you share a rough delta in $ / 1M between a streaming-first vs batching-first pilot?
2) If we commit to a 6-month reserved capacity, what discount bands apply?
3) For interactive caching (prefix/KV), do you support session-level cache pinning so we don't pay for repeated context?

We can confirm the QPS/concurrency numbers by Monday. If feasible, Ravi and I can do the Tue slot — prefer morning PST.

–Aisha
Aisha Patel
Head of Product, VeloxAI
Aisha.Patel@veloxai.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@veloxai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scoping: streaming vs batching economics and SLOs - post-call recap

Aisha — thanks for the fast turn. This is exactly what we need. Short answers and an outline of options; Grace and Vivek are looped for any technical clarifications.

Quick delta (high-level estimates)
- Streaming-first pilot (dedicated/high-priority hosted): expected $ / 1M tokens roughly $11–$14 depending on model family and quantization. Achieves ~200–350ms P95 for interactive flows with the concurrency numbers you gave (300 peak).
- Batching-first pilot (cost-optimized, mixed-quant run): expected $ / 1M tokens roughly $6–$9 depending on batch sizes and acceptance of higher tail latency (P95 ~500–900ms).
- Hybrid/multipath (recommended for your mix): route ~30% of traffic (interactive) to streaming endpoints and ~70% to batched paths. Blended $ / 1M tokens estimated $8.5–$11.5. We’ll produce a modeled table for your exact volume (fill the CSV).

Reserved capacity / discounts
- 6-month commit: typical discounts 10–18% depending on committed spend and model footprint; higher discounts available for annual heavy commits. We’ll run a concrete quote once you pick option A/B/Hybrid.

Caching and session pinning
- Yes: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching with session-affinity options for pinned contexts; that will reduce token costs on repeated context substantially. We’ll show a sensitivity column in the cost model for cache hit rates (0/25/50/75%).

Pilot proposal (next steps)
1) You confirm the CSV numbers by EOD Mon.
2) We produce two line-item pilot options + blended model by Tue morning.
3) 30-min sync Tue 10:00–10:30 PST to review. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

If you want, we can also include a short SLA addendum for the pilot that governs latency targets and fallback routing — useful if you want contractual visibility on P95.

Thanks — Grace/Vivek: can you validate the P95 ranges above and add any notes about model-variant compatibility for 4-bit quantization?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: scoping-notes.docx
